\- I detected and removed 37 distinct malicious backdoors. That number suggests the site was probably hacked by several parties.
\- The earliest attack files were uploaded in September, while all the malware spam posts arrived in October.
\- Given the severity, restoring a backup from an earlier point is the best approach. However, the earliest version available on WP-Engine was made on October 20th, and it is infected as well.
\- The removal is complete, but some issues remain with the page and post status.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports removing 37 malicious backdoors and states that malware removal is complete.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Current status: the site layout has been fully recovered, Wordfence has been configured for security, malware has been removed from around 34 outdated plugins, and all fake admins have been removed.

Follow-up work remains. Although the pages appear fine, I cannot verify whether all the private pages work correctly. Please test every contact form and change your admin password. For the search-engine cleanup, I still need Search Console access for Stonefield as well.

**Overall report**
There are signs of earlier, smaller-scale attacks dating back to 2022. The majority of the 14000 posts were injected on October 14th, and all of the website's pages were deleted on December 20th.

execution.observed_behavior: After restoration established a new cleanup baseline, the freelancer reports removing malware from around 34 outdated plugins.

source_message.text: We can probably conclude the remediation for this site as well, since WP Engine's internal scan has also given it a clean bill of health.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Removing the page builder now would break the current site because it does more than build pages; its features often control how those pages are styled and displayed. Full removal may therefore have to wait until the new site is ready.

As an interim step, I’ll disable Thrive Apprentice, which is the plugin providing the learning-platform functionality.

ambiguity.description: The freelancer recommends postponing full Thrive removal until the replacement site is ready, but the client has not explicitly confirmed that deferral.

human_review.reason: The source confirms that Thrive is used on the current site and absent from the replacement site, but it does not resolve whether the vulnerable installation should be updated, retained temporarily, or removed; propagation requires a further remediation decision.
